basis: Local static export of the 11,464-entry corpus on 2026-09-04, after the REL-01 quarantine. Owner approval and real-device measurement remain open, so this stays provisional.

/.note: Measured 203,422 bytes on 2026-09-04. Raised from 204,800, where the route had 0.67% headroom — 675 bytes, less than a paragraph of copy. A cap that tight makes an ordinary change into a budget negotiation, and the design migration in Phase 6 adds markup to every route. 240,000 leaves 15.2%, the margin marginPolicy asks for, and is a deliberate widening rather than a nudge to make one build pass.

/library/.note: Measured 220,212 bytes on 2026-09-04. Raised from 225,000 (2.13% headroom). This route has been operated at the edge twice: it sat at 99.76% of its cap during the 2026-09-01 audit and then exceeded it when correctness fixes landed. 260,000 leaves 15.3%. The lazily-loaded FacetsNotice from that episode is kept on its own merits, not as budget slack. Still provisional: never validated on a real device.

export.note: Measured 476,100,991 HTML bytes and 809,688,520 raw across 15,194 files on 2026-09-04. htmlBytes raised from 524,288,000, where the export had 0.014% headroom — roughly one more catalogue page before the build failed. 560,000,000 leaves 15.0%. rawBytes is deliberately NOT raised: 943,718,400 sits under a host site limit we do not control, so the correct response to pressure there is to ship fewer bytes, not to widen the cap. It has 14.2% headroom today. files has 15.6%.

marginPolicy.rationale: IMP-PERF-001. Both route budgets have been operated at the edge: /library/ was at 99.76% when the 2026-09-01 audit ran and exceeded its cap once correctness fixes landed, and / is at 0.85% headroom today. A cap that is only discovered at the moment it breaks turns ordinary work (compiler metadata, a copy change, a security fix) into an emergency budget negotiation. This states the intended operational margin once: below 5% headroom the build WARNS, loudly and every time, so the decision to trim bytes or widen the cap is made deliberately and early. It deliberately does NOT raise any cap - the audit's instruction was not to nudge thresholds without stating a margin, and a passing route must not be loosened speculatively.
